scene.speaker: nico
scene.bubble: N-I-C-O! Spelling your name is like a little song. How do you spell YOUR name?
scene.intro: N-I-C-O! Spelling your name is like a little song. How do you spell your name? asks Astrid, with her pencil ready. Nico spells it fast, too fast, and Astrid writes NIKO. Again, please — slowly! Letter by letter, they write every name in the class, and every surname too. How do YOU spell your name? Listen, say it slowly and write it down!

activities.title: Match the name with its spelling.
Quick check · Choose the correct spelling.
Listen and spell. Write a name in each gap.

data.script: Nico: Spelling game! The new boy's name is Leo. L-E-O. … Astrid: L-E-O. Leo. Got it! … Nico: The teacher's cat is called Misu. M-I-S-U. … Astrid: M-I-S-U. What a sweet name! … Nico: The boat at the port is called Rosa. R-O-S-A. … Astrid: R-O-S-A. Like a flower! … Nico: And the hardest one… the lighthouse name: FARO. F-A-R-O! … Astrid: All correct. Spelling champions!

items.sentence: To say a word letter by letter is to ___ it.
If you don't hear well, say: "___, please!"
When your friend spells well, say: "___!"

data.text: Spell your name and surname for your partner. They write it and show you. Correct? Now spell your favourite animal!

activities.title: Spot the differences!
activities.instructions: Look at picture A and picture B. Find the 12 differences and tell your partner about them.

homework.prompt: Write the names of 4 people in your family and spell them in letters: M-A-M-A…

outcomes.puede: Understand short simple dialogues about family, school, animals, food (Cambridge Starters Listening parts 1–4).
Answer picture-prompted questions; describe a picture in simple sentences.
Read 2–3-sentence texts; match pictures to words and short captions.
Copy words and complete short sentences (Starters Reading/Writing parts).
~450 words (Starters wordlist); Present simple, present continuous (limited), there is/are, like + -ing.
